wa: On-call—when on call for day and a night
Close call—when on close call for day and a night

Cold places[#b][#m]—An employee required to work for more than one hour in places where the temperature is reduced by artificial means below 0 degrees Celsius.[#m] Special conditions[#b][#i][#m] Where the work continues for more than two hours an employee is entitled to a rest period of 20 minutes every two hours without loss of pay.

Confined spaces[#b][#m]—An employee required to work in a confined space, as defined.[#m] “confined space” means a compartment, space or place the dimensions of which necessitate an employee working in a stooped or otherwise cramped position, or without proper ventilation.
Dirty work[#b][#m]—Where an employee and a supervisor agree that work is of an unusually dirty or offensive nature.

Height[#b][#m]—Employees engaged in the construction, erection, repair and/or maintenance of any structure over 15 metres, while working at a height of 15 metres or more directly above the nearest horizontal plane.
For each additional 15 metres distance above the ground:
Hot places[#b][#m]—An employee required to work for more than one hour in the shade in places where the temperature is raised by artificial means to between 46 and 54 Celsius.

Hot places[#b][#m]—An employee required to work for more than one hour in the shade in places where the temperature is raised by artificial means to between 46 and 54 Celsius.[#m] [#m] Special conditions[#b][#i][#m] Where work continues for more than two hours in temperatures exceeding 54 Celsius, employees will be entitled to 20 minutes rest after every two hours work without deduction of pay. The temperature will be determined by the supervisor after consultation with the employees who claim the extra rate.

Wet places[#b][#m]—An employee required to work in any place where clothing or boots become saturated by water, oil or another substance.[#m] Special conditions[#b][#i][#m] (1) Any employee who becomes entitled to this extra rate will be paid such rate only for the part of the day or shift that they are required to work in wet clothing or boots.[#m] (2) This extra rate is not payable to an employee who is provided by the employer with suitable and effective protective clothing and/or footwear.
Aquatic ponds[#b][#m]—An employee required to work in water in aquatic ponds.

Asbestos eradication[#b][#m]—Employees directly employed on asbestos eradication, where the wearing of protective equipment (i.e. combination overalls and breathing equipment or similar apparatus) is required.

Asbestos handling[#b][#m]—Employees required to use materials containing asbestos or to work in close proximity to employees using such materials, where the wearing of protective equipment (i.e. combination overalls and breathing equipment or similar apparatus) is required.
Barber-Greene operator[#b][#m]—Employees attached to a Barber-Greene machine spreading hot-mix.
Bitumen and asphalt[#b][#m]—An employee handling hot bitumen or asphalt or dipping materials in creosote.
Brick cleaning[#b][#m]—An employee required to clean down bricks using acids or other corrosive substances.
Brick cutting[#b][#m]—If on any site there is a brickcutting machine, only one bricklayer on that site will operate the cutting machine and will, whilst so engaged, be paid an allowance.
Cleaning economisers, etc.[#b][#m]—An employee required to work externally on economisers or boilers under fire (where temperature money is not paid), or on tractors or brickmaking machinery.
An employee required to work internally on economisers or boilers (where temperature money is not paid).

Construction/repairs to boilers, flues, etc[#b][#m]//An employee performing the duties of Bricklayer or Builder’s Labourer, engaged on the construction or alteration or repairs to boilers, flues, furnaces, retorts, kilns, ovens, ladles and similar refractory work or on acid furnaces, acid stills, acid towers and all other acid resisting brickwork.

Diesel engines – [#b][#m]—An employee performing repairs and renewals inside any crankcase.[#m] Payment for work performed other than in the crankcase will only occur when the employer considers it is warranted.[#i]
Dry polishing of tiles[#b][#m]—Employees engaged on dry polishing tiles where machines are used.
Epoxy-based materials – close proximity[#b][#m]—Employees required to work in close proximity to employees engaged on work under item 12 so as to be affected by the materials specified.

Epoxy-based materials – use [#b][#m]—Employees who use epoxy-based materials and all materials which include or require the addition of a catalyst hardener and reactive additives or two-pack catalyst system.
Explosive powered tools[#b][#m]—An operator of explosive powered tools, holding the appropriate certification, who is required to use an explosive powered tool.
Fumes[#b][#m]—An employee required to work in a place where fumes of sulphur or other acid or other offensive fumes are present.
Where the blocks weigh over 5.5kg and under 9kg
Where the blocks weigh 9kg or over and up to 18kg
Height work - painting trades:[#b][#m]—An employee working on any structure at a height of more than nine (9) metres where an adequate fixed support not less than 0.75 metres wide is not provided.
Insanitary / sewerage sludge[#b][#m]//An employee called upon to work in insanitary conditions or unload sewerage sludge.

Insulation[#b][#m]—An employee handling charcoal, pumice, granulated cork, silicate of cotton, insulwool, slag wool, limpet fibre, vermiculite, or other recognised insulating material of a like nature, associated with similar disabilities in its use.[#m] [#m] Special conditions[#b][#i][#m] This extra rate will also apply to an employee working in the immediate vicinity who is affected by the use of such materials.
Leadburning[#b][#m]—An employee performing trade level plumbing functions or apprentices to that trade engaged on lead burning.

Live sewer work[#b][#m]—‘Live sewer work’ means work carried out in situations where there is direct aerial connection with a sewer though which sewerage is flowing.[#m] Where aerial connection with such sewer is blocked by a disc, plug, water seal or other means the live sewer rate shall not apply. [#m] An employee in receipt of the live sewer rate shall not be entitled to the extra rate in item 15.
Plaster or composition[#b][#m]—An Employees using a plaster or composition spray.
Rain[#b][#m]—Employees who are required to work in rain.
Roof repairs[#b][#m]—Employees engaged on repairs to roofs.
Second hand timber[#b][#m]—Where, whilst working with second-hand timber, an employee’s tools are damaged by nails, dumps or other foreign matter on the timber.
Sewerage pit work[#b][#m]—An employee employed on work which involves entering a sewerage pit for the purpose of servicing, disconnecting and/or removal or replacement of electrical equipment.
Sewerage tunnels[#b][#m]—Employees cleaning chokeage in pumps conveying sewerage or working in sewerage tunnels.
Spray gangs[#b][#m]—Employees engaged in spray gangs on destruction of weeds and/or vermin.
Employees using high pressure sprays for this purpose
Spraypainting[#b][#m]—An employee performing trade level painting functions engaged on all spray painting carried out in other than a properly constructed booth.

Swing scaffold[#b][#m]—An employee required to work from any type of swing scaffold or any scaffold suspended by rope or cable, bosun’s chair, or a suspended scaffold requiring the use of steel or iron hooks or angle irons.
per day for first four hours
per hour for fifth and subsequent hours
Tile cutting[#b][#m]—An employee engaged at cutting tiles by electric saw.
Trenches[#b][#m]—An employee required to work in trenches deeper than 1.8 metres and less than 0.9 metres in width.

Underground[#b][#m]—An employee required to work underground.[#m] Where a shaft is to be sunk to a depth greater than 6 metres, the payment of the underground allowance will commence from the surface.[#i]
Unsewered toilet[#b][#m]—Any employee, other than a lavatory attendant or street cleaner, called upon to attend at unsewered toilets.
Unusually obnoxious work[#b][#m]—Work involving offensive and/or obnoxious material.
Window cleaning[#b][#m]—An employee required to work on the outside of multi-storey buildings from scaffolds or similar devices.
when working at a height exceeding 12 metres, but not exceeding 24 metres above the ground or nearest horizontal plane[#p]
when working at a height exceeding 24 metres, but not exceeding 60 metres above the ground or nearest horizontal plane[#p]
when working at a height exceeding 60 metres from the ground or nearest horizontal plane[#p]
Working aloft - trees[#b][#m]—An employee who is required to climb trees to a height greater than 6 metres from the ground.
